newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo cen.bank plans to sweep away internal debts.
newsitem.headline: Yugo cen.bank plans to sweep away internal debts.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank, worried by the alarming increase in the internal debts, plans to sweep them away using a general programme of so-called "multilateral compensations", central bank vice-governor Ratko Banovic told Reuters on Friday.

Internal debts rose by 5.8 percent to reach the alarming 3.988 billion dinars ($819.3 million) at the end of July when M1 money supply stood at 4.34 billion dinars, the IZIT Institute for Market Research said earlier this week.

"We have to take some action to annul all internal debts and give banks and companies a breathing space, but we have to work it out carefully in order not to have one single debtor when the operation is over," Banovic said.

According to Banovic, the programme needs to function as a closed circle. "Otherwise, if we had one single debtor left, we would have to print money to compensate the losses, and we do not want to risk that."
According to Banovic, the M1 money supply accounted for some 10 percent of the country's gross domestic product. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
